si_4_title: Adjustment of Regional Cortical Thickness Measures for Global Cortical Thickness Obscures Deficits Across the Schizophrenia Spectrum: A Cautionary Note About Normative Modeling of Brain Imaging Data

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Study 1 used an archival dataset from the University of California San Francisco (UCSF), which corresponds to a single-site dataset. Study 2 used data from the Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCP-EP).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: Study 1 included healthy control participants (HCs), participants at CHR-P, and participants with early-illness schizophrenia (ESZ) who underwent MRI scanning at the University of California San Francisco. Study 2 included HCs, participants with nonaffective psychosis (NAff-P), and participants with affective psychosis (Aff-P) who underwent MRI scanning as part of the HCP-EP (Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Hua2025.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Study 1 Participants & Study 2 Participants

answer.SINGLE-SITE: normative training and testing for Study 1 model; patient for clinical research (CHR-P, ESZ)

answer.HCP-EP: normative training and testing for Study 2 model; patient for clinical research (NAff-P, Aff-P)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy controls (HCs) from both datasets were used to build the normative models (regression) and served as the reference group (test). Patients from the schizophrenia spectrum were used to evaluate the impact of global thickness adjustment on regional thickness deficits.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: ROI thicknesses were regressed on age, gender, and site (only study 2 included site) in HCs to model the effects of normal aging, gender, and site. Resulting parameter estimates were used to derive predicted ROI values for each participant, irrespective of group, which reflected the expected thickness for a healthy individual of a specific age, gender, and site.

dc_3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norm.detail: The study utilized two cohorts to build normative models. Study 1 used 90 HCs and Study 2 used 56 HCs. The same HCs were used for model fitting (training) and as the baseline comparison group (overall phase).
